quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The regulator's supervisory engagement with a mid-tier insurer identified concerns that the firm's internal model for calculating regulatory capital requirements was producing outputs inconsistent with its risk profile and with comparators in the market. The regulator opened an internal model application review. The review found that several key assumptions in the model were insufficiently conservative and directed the firm to implement a range of model adjustments.
options: Supervisory engagement found the insurer's internal capital model was producing inconsistent outputs.
The regulator opened an internal model application review.
The review found insufficiently conservative assumptions and directed model adjustments.
The review found the internal model was appropriately calibrated and approved it without change.
quests.hint: Follow the supervisory story: identifying the model concern, opening a review, then the finding and direction. One frame approves the model without change.
quests.explanation: Prudential regulation narratives show identifying a modelling concern, opening a review, and finding inadequate assumptions requiring adjustments. The distractor approves without change.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: A community heritage trust commissioned an architectural historian to assess the historical significance of a group of post-war prefabricated housing units that were being considered for demolition as part of a regeneration programme. The assessment found the units represented the only surviving example of a particular construction system developed in the late nineteen forties and recommended that the group be listed. The trust submitted the assessment to the national heritage body which accepted the recommendation and listed the buildings.
options: The heritage body found insufficient grounds for listing and the units were demolished.
An architectural historian was commissioned to assess post-war prefabricated housing units for historical significance.
The assessment found them the only surviving example of a late nineteen forties construction system.
The heritage body accepted the recommendation and listed the buildings.
quests.hint: Trace: the assessment finding, the recommendation to list, then the heritage body accepting. One frame has the buildings demolished.
quests.explanation: Heritage listing narratives show a significance assessment, a listing recommendation, and heritage body acceptance. The distractor demolishes the buildings.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The family court considered an application for a child arrangements order in proceedings where one parent alleged the other had perpetrated coercive and controlling behaviour during the relationship. The court conducted a fact-finding hearing and found, on the balance of probabilities, that coercive control had been established. It ordered a risk assessment before determining the final arrangements.
options: The family court conducted a fact-finding on alleged coercive control by one parent.
It found coercive control was established on the balance of probabilities.
The court found the coercive control allegations were not established on the evidence.
It ordered a risk assessment before determining final child arrangements.
quests.hint: Sequence: the fact-finding, the finding of coercive control, then ordering a risk assessment. One frame finds the allegations unestablished.
quests.explanation: Family court narratives show a fact-finding hearing, a finding on the balance of probabilities, and ordering a risk assessment. The distractor finds the allegations unestablished.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The equality regulator published a statutory code of practice on the duty to make reasonable adjustments for disabled people in employment. The code included new guidance on anticipatory duties requiring employers to put in place adjustments before they are requested. Three major employers issued updated workplace adjustment policies within six months citing the code.
options: The equality regulator published a code on reasonable adjustments including new anticipatory duty guidance.
All major employers said existing policies were already compliant with the anticipatory duty guidance.
Three major employers issued updated adjustment policies within six months citing the code.
A new employer reporting requirement on adjustment take-up was included in the revised code.
quests.hint: Follow the policy story: publishing the code with anticipatory duty guidance, employers updating policies, then the new reporting requirement. One frame removes the reporting requirement.
quests.explanation: Equality code narratives show publishing a code, employer policy updates, and a new reporting requirement. The distractor removes the reporting requirement by claiming existing compliance.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The public accounts committee published a highly critical report on the implementation of a major social security IT system after finding that the project had been delivered in phases, each of which had required significant rework due to changing policy requirements being implemented during build. It found that the absence of a stable policy baseline before development began had been the root cause of the cost and time overruns. It recommended that future major digital programmes adopt an assured policy stability gateway before procurement begins.
options: The committee found cost and time overruns were caused by changing policy during system build.
It found the absence of a stable policy baseline before development was the root cause.
It recommended an assured policy stability gateway before future digital procurement begins.
The committee found the cost and time overruns were caused by contractor underperformance.
quests.hint: Trace: the root cause finding, the absence of baseline finding, then the gateway recommendation. One frame replaces the root cause with contractor underperformance.
quests.explanation: Programme accountability narratives show finding a root cause, identifying the absence of a stable baseline, and recommending a gateway. The distractor blames the contractor instead.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The senior caseworker at a housing charity identified that several clients had been denied emergency housing assistance because the local authority's gatekeeping process required them to demonstrate a local connection that they could not prove due to having fled domestic abuse. She submitted a super-complaint to the housing ombudsman. The ombudsman found the gatekeeping practice unlawful and ordered the authority to pay backdated housing support to all affected clients.
options: The housing ombudsman found the connection requirement was a lawful exercise of the authority's discretion.
The caseworker found clients fleeing abuse were denied housing due to an unlawful connection requirement.
She submitted a super-complaint to the housing ombudsman.
The ombudsman found the gatekeeping unlawful and ordered backdated support for all clients.
quests.hint: Sequence: identifying unlawful gatekeeping, the super-complaint, then the ombudsman's finding and order. One frame finds the gatekeeping lawful.
quests.explanation: Housing law narratives show identifying an unlawful practice, a super-complaint, and an ombudsman finding of unlawfulness and ordering redress. The distractor finds the practice lawful.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The financial reporting review panel raised queries with the directors of a company about the accounting treatment it had adopted for a portfolio of lease contracts which it had classified as short-term leases exempt from the recognition requirements of the applicable accounting standard. The panel found the classification was incorrect and required the company to restate its accounts. The restatement added significant lease liabilities to the balance sheet.
options: The review panel challenged the company's short-term lease classification as exempt from recognition.
It found the classification was incorrect and required a restatement.
The panel accepted the short-term lease classification and found the accounts were accurate.
The restatement added significant lease liabilities to the balance sheet.
quests.hint: Follow the accounting review: the query, the finding of incorrect classification, then the restatement impact. One frame accepts the classification.
quests.explanation: Financial reporting review narratives show challenging a classification, finding it incorrect, and requiring a balance sheet restatement. The distractor accepts the classification.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The social enterprise's board of trustees received a report showing that two of its three trading subsidiaries were generating losses that were being cross-subsidised from its core charitable reserves, in breach of charity law restrictions on applying charitable funds to benefit non-charitable activities. The board resolved to restructure the group so that the subsidiaries either achieved viability or were wound up. Both subsidiaries were wound up within four months.
options: Trustees found two loss-making subsidiaries were being cross-subsidised from charitable reserves unlawfully.
The board found the cross-subsidy was permissible as an investment in the charity's wider mission.
The board resolved to restructure so subsidiaries achieved viability or were wound up.
Both subsidiaries were wound up within four months.
quests.hint: Trace: finding the unlawful cross-subsidy, resolving to restructure or wind up, then winding up. One frame finds the cross-subsidy permissible.
quests.explanation: Charity governance narratives show finding unlawful cross-subsidy, resolving to restructure, and winding up the subsidiaries. The distractor finds the cross-subsidy permissible.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The environmental health officer inspected a food processing facility following a complaint from a former employee alleging that temperature monitoring records had been falsified. She found evidence that logs had been altered and that a batch of cooked meat products had been released without the required cooling time being achieved. She issued an immediate prohibition notice. The company recalled the affected products.
options: The officer found temperature logs had been falsified and an inadequately cooled batch had been released.
She issued an immediate prohibition notice.
The company recalled the affected products.
The officer found the temperature records were accurate and the products met food safety standards.
quests.hint: Sequence: finding falsified records and a released inadequate batch, the prohibition notice, then the recall. One frame finds the records accurate.
quests.explanation: Food safety enforcement narratives show finding falsified records, issuing a prohibition notice, and a product recall. The distractor finds the records accurate.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The specialist financial crimes unit used network analysis of transaction data to identify a web of connected accounts through which criminal proceeds were being layered using structured cash deposits designed to fall below the reporting threshold. It sought and obtained account freezing orders against twenty-seven accounts across nine institutions. Cash equivalent to four million pounds was subsequently forfeited.
options: The network analysis found the transactions were consistent with legitimate business activity.
Network analysis identified structured deposits used to layer criminal proceeds below the reporting threshold.
Account freezing orders were obtained against twenty-seven accounts across nine institutions.
Cash equivalent to four million pounds was subsequently forfeited.
quests.hint: Follow the money laundering story: identifying the structured deposits, obtaining freezing orders, then the forfeiture. One frame clears the accounts.
quests.explanation: Financial crime narratives show network analysis finding layering, obtaining freezing orders, and forfeiture. The distractor clears the accounts.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The land registration authority received an application for first registration of a property and identified that the title deeds submitted contained a forged signature purporting to be that of the registered proprietor of an adjacent parcel whose land the applicant's conveyance purported to include. The authority referred the matter to its fraud team. The fraud team found that the forged document formed part of a series of fraudulent conveyances and referred the matter to the police.
options: First registration documents were found to contain a forged signature on the adjacent parcel's conveyance.
The authority referred the matter to its fraud team.
The authority accepted the title deeds as authentic and completed the first registration.
The fraud team found serial fraudulent conveyances and referred the matter to the police.
quests.hint: Trace: identifying the forgery, referring to the fraud team, then finding serial fraud and police referral. One frame accepts the forged deeds.
quests.explanation: Land registration fraud narratives show identifying a forgery, referring to the fraud team, and finding serial fraudulent conveyances. The distractor accepts the forgery.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The high court considered a contempt of court application in which it was alleged that a party to civil litigation had destroyed documents subject to a litigation hold notice. The court found, on the criminal standard of proof, that destruction had been deliberate and in bad faith. It imposed a substantial fine, costs on the indemnity basis, and a specific disclosure order.
options: The court considered a contempt application for deliberate destruction of documents under a litigation hold.
The court found the destruction was accidental and dismissed the contempt application.
It found, on the criminal standard, that destruction was deliberate and in bad faith.
It imposed a fine, indemnity costs, and a specific disclosure order.
quests.hint: Sequence: the contempt application, the finding of deliberate bad faith destruction, then the penalties. One frame finds the destruction accidental.
quests.explanation: Contempt of court narratives show a contempt application, finding deliberate bad faith on the criminal standard, and imposing a range of penalties. The distractor finds the destruction accidental.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The county court considered a claim for fraudulent misrepresentation against a vendor of a commercial property who had disclosed that the property was free from environmental contamination while knowing that an earlier environmental survey had identified hydrocarbon contamination on part of the site. The court found the non-disclosure amounted to fraudulent misrepresentation. It rescinded the contract and ordered damages representing the cost of remediation.
options: A vendor had failed to disclose known hydrocarbon contamination while representing the site was clean.
The court found the non-disclosure amounted to fraudulent misrepresentation.
The contract was rescinded and remediation costs were awarded as damages.
The court found the vendor had made reasonable enquiries and the non-disclosure was not fraudulent.
quests.hint: Follow the property fraud story: the non-disclosure, the finding of fraudulent misrepresentation, then rescission and damages. One frame removes the fraud finding.
quests.explanation: Property fraud narratives show a non-disclosure, a finding of fraudulent misrepresentation, and rescission with damages. The distractor finds the non-disclosure not fraudulent.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The housing developer's planning consultant reviewed an appeal decision and identified that the inspector had failed to apply the sequential and exception tests required by national planning policy before dismissing the appeal on flood risk grounds for a site in flood zone two. She lodged an application for costs against the local planning authority for unreasonable behaviour in maintaining a flood risk reason for refusal that could not withstand scrutiny. The inspector awarded costs in full.
options: The inspector upheld the flood risk reason and dismissed the costs application.
The consultant found the inspector had not applied the required sequential and exception tests.
She lodged an application for costs against the authority for unreasonable behaviour.
The inspector awarded full costs.
quests.hint: Trace: identifying the inspector's failure, applying for costs, then the full award. One frame upholds the flood risk reason and dismisses costs.
quests.explanation: Planning appeal narratives show identifying an inspector's failure, applying for costs, and a full costs award. The distractor upholds the inspector and dismisses costs.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The public inquiry into historical institutional child abuse received testimony from more than eight hundred survivors over three years of hearings. Its final report documented systemic failures in regulatory oversight, inadequate vetting of staff, and cultures of disbelief that had silenced victims. It made ninety-seven recommendations directed at government, regulatory bodies, and care institutions.
options: The inquiry received testimony from more than eight hundred survivors over three years.
Its final report documented systemic failures in oversight, vetting, and cultures of disbelief.
The inquiry found the abuse was the result of individual misconduct rather than systemic failure.
It made ninety-seven recommendations directed at government, regulators, and institutions.
quests.hint: Sequence: the inquiry, the final report's systemic findings, then the recommendations. One frame limits findings to individual misconduct.
quests.explanation: Institutional abuse inquiry narratives show extensive testimony, systemic findings, and wide-ranging recommendations. The distractor limits the findings to individual misconduct.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The employment tribunal considered a whistleblower claim in which the claimant alleged that she had been subjected to a series of detriments after making protected disclosures about the company's accounting practices. The tribunal found that the decision-makers had been motivated partly by the protected disclosures and partly by interpersonal conflict, and that the whistleblowing element was a materially significant cause. It upheld the claim and awarded compensation.
options: The tribunal found decision-makers had been motivated partly by protected disclosures and partly by personal conflict.
The tribunal found the detriments were motivated entirely by interpersonal conflict unrelated to the disclosures.
The tribunal found the whistleblowing was a materially significant cause of the detriments.
It upheld the claim and awarded compensation.
quests.hint: Follow the whistleblower story: the mixed motivation finding, materiality, then upholding and compensating. One frame removes the disclosure motivation.
quests.explanation: Whistleblower detriment narratives show finding mixed motivation, identifying the disclosure as material, and upholding the claim. The distractor removes the disclosure motivation.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The judicial review of a central government department's decision to close a network of publicly accessible gender-based violence support centres in rural areas was brought by a coalition of survivor advocacy groups. The court found that the department had failed to conduct the public sector equality duty assessment required before making the decision. The decision was quashed and the department was required to conduct a lawful equality analysis before any further closure decisions.
options: A JR challenged closure of rural gender-based violence centres without a public sector equality duty assessment.
The court found the department had failed to conduct the required PSED assessment.
The decision was quashed and a lawful equality analysis required before further closures.
The court found the equality duty analysis had been adequately conducted before the closure decision.
quests.hint: Trace: the JR ground, the court's PSED finding, then quashing and requiring a lawful analysis. One frame finds the PSED adequately conducted.
quests.explanation: PSED judicial review narratives show challenging a decision for failing the equality duty, a finding of failure, and quashing. The distractor finds the duty adequately conducted.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The accountant in practice was engaged to prepare financial statements for a small business and identified that the owner had been systematically withdrawing cash from the business and recording the withdrawals as business expenses. She discussed the matter with the owner and formed the view that the explanation provided was not credible. She resigned from the engagement and submitted a suspicious activity report to the National Crime Agency.
options: She accepted the owner's explanation and completed the financial statements as instructed.
The accountant identified systematic cash withdrawals being misrecorded as business expenses.
She found the owner's explanation was not credible.
She resigned and submitted a suspicious activity report to the NCA.
quests.hint: Sequence: finding misrecording, finding the explanation not credible, then resigning and reporting. One frame accepts the explanation and completes the statements.
quests.explanation: Professional ethics narratives show finding fraud, finding the explanation not credible, and resigning while reporting. The distractor accepts the explanation and continues.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The court of protection authorised a local authority to obtain a capacity assessment and mental health assessment for a man with severe dementia who was living in circumstances that raised serious concerns about self-neglect and exploitation by family members. The assessments confirmed that he lacked capacity to make decisions about his residence and care. The court authorised placement in a registered care home.
options: The court authorised a capacity and mental health assessment for a man with dementia in concerning circumstances.
The assessments confirmed he lacked capacity for decisions about his residence and care.
The court found the man had capacity and refused to authorise any interference with his choices.
The court authorised placement in a registered care home.
quests.hint: Follow the court of protection story: authorising the assessments, the capacity finding, then authorising placement. One frame finds capacity and refuses interference.
quests.explanation: Court of protection narratives show authorising assessments, finding lack of capacity, and authorising protective placement. The distractor finds capacity and refuses intervention.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The infrastructure manager's safety case review identified that a deteriorating concrete viaduct carrying an electrified railway had not been subject to a principal inspection for fourteen years and that its risk assessment was based on assumptions about the asset's condition that were no longer supportable. It commissioned a specialist structural inspection. The inspection found extensive carbonation and chloride-induced corrosion requiring immediate partial closure and accelerated repair.
options: A review found the viaduct had not had a principal inspection for fourteen years on unsupportable assumptions.
The specialist inspection found the viaduct remained in sound structural condition.
A specialist structural inspection was commissioned.
The inspection found extensive corrosion requiring immediate partial closure and accelerated repair.
quests.hint: Trace: the safety case review finding, commissioning the inspection, then the corrosion finding. One frame finds the structure sound.
quests.explanation: Infrastructure safety narratives show identifying an inspection gap, commissioning a specialist survey, and finding serious corrosion requiring closure. The distractor finds the structure sound.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The public health authority identified a cluster of listeriosis cases with an epidemiological link to a ready-to-eat food product supplied to a national sandwich chain. Whole genome sequencing of isolates from cases and from samples of the product confirmed they were genetically indistinguishable. A product recall was issued and the production facility was suspended pending inspection. The inspection found persistent contamination from a brine pipe leaking into the production environment.
options: A listeriosis cluster was epidemiologically linked to a ready-to-eat food product.
Whole genome sequencing confirmed genetic indistinguishability between patient and product isolates.
A recall and facility suspension led to the discovery of persistent brine pipe contamination.
The genome sequencing found the patient isolates were genetically distinct from the product samples.
quests.hint: Sequence: the cluster and epidemiological link, whole genome confirmation, then recall and contamination discovery. One frame removes the genetic link.
quests.explanation: Outbreak investigation narratives show an epidemiological link, genome sequencing confirmation, and recall leading to source discovery. The distractor removes the genetic link.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The asset manager identified that a fund it managed had a concentration of illiquid assets representing sixty per cent of net asset value, significantly exceeding the thirty per cent limit in the fund's prospectus. It applied to the regulator for an extension of the suspension of dealing in the fund. The regulator granted a ninety-day extension while requiring the manager to submit a liquidity management plan within thirty days.

quests.explanation: Fund regulation narratives show identifying a concentration breach, applying for a suspension extension, and a conditional grant. The distractor refuses the extension.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The mental health tribunal reviewed the detention of a patient who had been compulsorily admitted under section two of the Mental Health Act and was applying for discharge. Medical evidence before the tribunal indicated that the patient had responded well to medication and that their mental state had improved significantly. The tribunal found that the criteria for detention were no longer met and ordered discharge with a community care package.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The forensic linguist was engaged to analyse disputed authorship of a series of threatening messages that had been attributed to a defendant. She applied both stylometric analysis and a comparison of idiolectal features across the disputed and reference texts. Her analysis found a high degree of similarity in lexical, syntactic, and pragmatic features and she expressed a positive opinion of shared authorship. The defendant was convicted.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.

She conducted a rapid practice review identifying the most significant areas of concern. quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
